title: Brand Foundation & Mockup Review
format: Video call — brand walkthrough + round-2 mockup review
tldr: Brandon paused the build to nail the brand backbone first — and came in with real clarity. The name is confirmed: Vital Alignments, with a Hawaiian tagline meaning "live well," a one-sentence pitch, mission, target audience, problem and result all written out. He listed his service lineup and described the site as a landing page that funnels visitors to "book an appointment," backed by blog + YouTube content. He's bought into vitalalignments.com (hit a minor login snag, parked it). On look: earth tones — sand, ocean, volcanic rock, wood/trees, sunrise/sunset — "Apple meets holistic human performance," minimal/elegant/cinematic/grounded, not techy/neon/sterile. He reviewed the round-2 mockups: liked Coastal Sanctuary (#1) and Rooted Expression (#3, loved the relief→restore→integrate→optimize care journey); cooled on Vital Precision (#2, too techy / too "Dr. Bueller"); liked Living Waters' green-blue depth but wants to kill the orange CTA and drop the Hawaiian-word copy. Logo is paused (he's chasing an old Fuji-bike logo for inspiration, likes a wave+mountain mark). Next: Top Rock generates a round 3 from this feedback.

actionItems.action: Send a photo of his handwritten notes/checklist (the foundational brand content).
Track down the old Fuji-bike logo detail for logo inspiration.
Log this feedback and generate a round 3 of three mockups.
Try non-orange CTA colors and the soft-green/ocean palette.
Keep email capture / newsletter in the design.
Schedule a July lunch when Brandon is in town (meet Austin in person).
